questions.question: What is Node.js?
options: A new programming language compiled to JavaScript
A JavaScript runtime built on V8 that adds APIs for files, networking and processes
A browser engine without a user interface
A JavaScript framework for building web pages
questions.explanation: Node is a runtime: V8 runs the JavaScript, libuv handles I/O, and core modules expose system APIs.

questions.question: Which component of Node.js parses, compiles and runs your JavaScript code?
questions.explanation: V8 is Google's JavaScript engine, the same one used in Chrome.

questions.question: Which component provides Node's event loop and the thread pool used for file system operations?
questions.explanation: libuv is the C library that implements the event loop, async I/O and the worker pool.

questions.question: Which of these exist as globals in Node.js? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: window and document are browser-only. process, fetch and globalThis exist in Node.

questions.question: In the restaurant analogy, why can a single Node thread serve many clients at once?
options: It runs all clients' code in parallel on every CPU core
It caches every response so no waiting is needed
It starts I/O and moves on, handling each result when it is ready, instead of waiting
It creates a new thread for each client automatically
questions.explanation: Non-blocking I/O: the single 'waiter' never stands still waiting for the 'kitchen' (the OS and libuv).

questions.question: Which kind of work is Node's single main thread worst at?
options: Serving thousands of idle WebSocket connections
questions.explanation: CPU-bound work blocks the only JavaScript thread; I/O waiting does not.

questions.question: Which Node release lines become Long-Term Support (LTS) releases?
questions.explanation: Even majors are promoted to LTS in October; odd majors are Current-only and never LTS.

questions.question: What does a .nvmrc file in a project folder contain?
options: The Node version the project expects, read by version managers
questions.explanation: Version managers like nvm and fnm read .nvmrc (or .node-version) to switch to the project's Node version.

questions.question: Why is a JavaScript micro-benchmark that times only the first few calls of a function misleading?
options: Timers are inaccurate for the first second of a process
The first calls always run on a slower thread
Node caches function results after the first call
V8 first interprets code and only optimises 'hot' functions after many calls
questions.explanation: V8's tiered compilation (Ignition, then TurboFan) means early runs are slower than steady-state runs.

questions.question: A browser developer asks why they no longer need Babel for a Node 26 backend. What is the best answer?
options: Node translates all JavaScript to ES5 automatically
You choose the Node version you deploy, so you can use every feature it supports natively
Node ignores syntax it doesn't understand
questions.explanation: In the browser you can't control users' versions; on a server the runtime version is your decision.

questions.question: Which console method writes to standard error (stderr)?
questions.explanation: console.error and console.warn write to stderr; log, info, table go to stdout.

questions.question: Why should a command-line tool print diagnostics (progress, warnings) to stderr rather than stdout?
options: Because stdout is only for errors
So that piping or redirecting the tool's output passes only the real data
Because stderr is faster than stdout
Because stderr is shown in a different colour
questions.explanation: Separating data (stdout) from diagnostics (stderr) makes tools composable with pipes and redirects.

questions.question: Which is the safest way to end a CLI script with a failure code without cutting off pending output?

questions.explanation: process.exit() terminates immediately and may lose pending writes; exitCode lets Node finish its work first.

questions.question: Which command runs app.js with variables loaded from a .env file, without any npm package?

questions.question: Your tool asks two questions with readline/promises' question() and works in a terminal, but hangs when the answers are piped in. Why?

question() only works with TTYs and throws otherwise
Piped input is read as binary
questions.explanation: With piped stdin, readline consumes all lines immediately; use the async line iterator to buffer them.
